title: Review: The Study Log
explanation: **Level 2 review!** A study app logs each session: the student, the subject, minutes studied, and their quiz score after. Answer each question with one pipe chain. There's nothing new here, just everything from Level 2: the pipe, select, filter, arrange and mutate.

tasks.prompt: Keep only the Biology sessions, with just the student and score columns. Store it in result.
Find the 3 lowest scores: sort by score, smallest first, and keep 3 rows. Store it in result.
Math sessions only: add points_per_min (score ÷ minutes, rounded to 2), sort by score largest first, and keep student, score and points_per_min. Store it in result.
hints: Put each step on its own line, ending each line with |>.
tasks.answer: result <- study_log |> filter(subject == "Math") |> mutate(points_per_min = round(score / minutes, 2)) |> arrange(desc(score)) |> select(student, score, points_per_min)

tasks.prompt: Last one: across all subjects, keep sessions with points_per_min above 2, biggest first, showing student, subject and points_per_min. Store it in result.
hints: You need to make the column with mutate before you can filter on it.
tasks.answer: result <- study_log |> mutate(points_per_min = round(score / minutes, 2)) |> filter(points_per_min > 2) |> arrange(desc(points_per_min)) |> select(student, subject, points_per_min)

recap: Level 2 done! You can chain select, filter, arrange and mutate with the pipe to answer real questions in one readable recipe. Next up: summarising with group_by.
